doc.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022

chapter: Michael, influences and the Brecker Brothers
title: Why bands break up; solo careers versus the name
summary: Money and egos split bands, but the Brecker Brothers name overshadowed solo work.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: With everybody being a first call musician on their axes, is that partly why bands break up?

Well you know we never had that problem but from what I understand if there’s big money involved I think that’s why bands somehow break up, from what I’ve heard from other sources and scenes, although I’ve never really been through that myself. But you hear, once again, stories through the grapevine that money can easily get in the way and people think they’re being cheated and they’re not getting paid as much as the next guy. But you know if they’re great players everyone wants to have his say musically I think, that’s a big part of it. And then there are certain bands that know if they did break up full time like The Rolling Stones that they’d probably never get to the point where they have gotten, and they’ve all done solo records. And both Mike and I did solo records too. I would say his were far more successful than mine, but never — when we got together that was always a more special thing. We could never overcome the Brecker Brothers either name or just the image, no matter what we did alone.
